verdict: Xylem's revenue slipped 3% to $2.2 billion on project timing and cautious customer spending, but tighter costs lifted operating profit 15% to $385 million — even so, Xylem cut its full-year outlook and announced divestitures to focus the portfolio.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: -3% vs a year ago, flat organically

segments.name: Water Infrastructure
segments.note: Pumps and treatment equipment that move and clean water for utilities.

segments.name: Applied Water
segments.note: Pumps and systems for commercial buildings and industry — the quarter's growth engine. Xylem plans to sell this segment's international business.

segments.name: Measurement and Control Solutions
segments.note: Smart meters and analytics that measure water use and find leaks — revenue fell mainly because businesses were sold.

segments.name: Water Solutions and Services
segments.note: Water treatment and services, including for industrial customers.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative expenses
opex.note: Selling products and running the company day to day.

opex.name: Research and development expenses
opex.note: Developing pumps, meters and water-treatment technology.

opex.name: Restructuring and asset impairment charges
opex.note: Costs of reshaping the business and writing down assets.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $21M and a $5M loss on selling businesses, partly offset by $6M of other non-operating income — a net $20M cost.
oneTimers: Restructuring and asset impairment charges were $8M in the quarter, down from $23M a year ago.

A $5M loss on the sale of businesses (versus $37M a year ago) sits below operating income; adjusted EPS of $1.44 excludes that loss, restructuring, purchase-accounting amortization and special charges, which included IEEPA tariff refunds.

takeaways.title: Orders outran sales
takeaways.text: Orders rose 7% to $2.33B (up 10% organically) even as revenue fell — customers are delaying project spending decisions, not cancelling the work.

takeaways.title: Margins expanded
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 23.9%, up 70 basis points, as productivity savings and pricing beat inflation and lower volumes; operating margin rose to 17.5% from 14.7%.

takeaways.title: Guidance cut, portfolio slimmed
takeaways.text: Full-year revenue guidance fell to about $8.95B and adjusted EPS to $5.40–$5.45 (from $5.55–$5.70), and Xylem will sell Applied Water International and Specialty Flow Control and move from four segments to three in 2027.

footerNote: Net income is the consolidated $288M; $291M was attributable to Xylem after a $3M loss attributable to noncontrolling interests. Xylem reported four segments in Q3 2026; its planned three-segment structure for 2027 (including an Integrated Solutions and Services segment) had not yet taken effect.
